title: Manhattan plot

blocks.what_we_do: Draw a Manhattan plot of the association results along the autosomes. The plot reads the summary statistics file made at step 6.8.
blocks.why:
A [Manhattan plot](../docs/glossary.md#manhattan-plot) shows every tested variant as one point. The horizontal axis shows the chromosome and the position. The vertical axis shows -log10(p), so stronger results are higher. Nearby high points are often correlated through LD, so they may be one single signal. The position tells us where the evidence is, not which gene causes the effect.

All positions use the [GRCh38](../docs/glossary.md#grch38) genome build. The plot gives alternate chromosomes different colours. The chromosome labels and the order of the positions give the same information, so colour is not the only clue.
blocks.you_need: The summary statistics file from step 6.8. If R says that the file is missing, run step 6.8 first.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-3}
stats <- guided_summary_stats(cfg)
plot_data <- data.frame(CHROM = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(stats$chromosome)),
  POS = stats$base_pair_location, P = stats$p_value)
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.3", "manhattan.png"), function() plot_manhattan(plot_data, "Simulated GWAS: age, sex and ten PCs"))
stopifnot(sum(stats$p_value[valid_p(stats$p_value)] < 5e-8) == 8L)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R chunk is the complete command.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
There are three strong regions, on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12. Together they hold eight variants below 5e-8. The moderate region that we planted does not reach this usual threshold. Tests on the sex chromosomes and MT stay in the result table, but this figure shows only the autosomes. R saves the picture as a PNG file and prints its path. It does not show the picture in the console. To see it, open the file from the Files pane of RStudio (click the file name, then choose "View File").

The tested PLINK version is set in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: the executable chunks, the comparisons with the expected results and the final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file that R names and the previous step. Keep the command and the messages from the console. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Do four nearby significant variants always mean four independent causal effects?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Because of LD, several tested variants can point to the same single signal.

</details>

start_dir <- setwd(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else "..")
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
setwd(start_dir)

figures.gemini_prompt: Draw a schematic Manhattan plot with clearly labelled chromosomes and the conventional 5e-8 line. Mark a group of correlated points as one region, and state that a peak does not identify a causal gene. Do not invent gene annotations.
figures.alt_text: Autosomal association peaks exceed the conventional threshold on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12.
